market_frame: Domestic household energy in a single national market with a regulated default price that is reset quarterly by a public regulator, competing fixed-term and wholesale-linked alternatives, and adjacent home-energy hardware (electric vehicle charging, rooftop generation, storage, low-carbon heating) whose economics depend on the electricity contract and on the meter installed.

jobs.statement: When the regulated default rate moves and the bill changes, help a bill payer choose between locking a price and staying flexible while they cannot absorb an unpredictable bill and cannot easily check a comparison.

When home charging becomes the largest part of the electricity bill, help a driver get the cheapest reliable charging cost while their car or charge point limits which smart contracts work and an existing payment-for-export arrangement must survive the change.

When a generation owner suspects their payments for exported units are below market, help them work out whether metered payment beats a guaranteed legacy payment while metering, eligibility and a physical installation stand in the way.

When a heating system is near the end of its life and public grant money is available, help an owner-occupier decide whether low-carbon heating will work in their house and what it will really cost to run, while whole-system cost and disruption are unclear.

When a household wants a cheaper time-varying rate or metered export payment but does not have the metering for it, help them decide whether accepting a new meter is worth it while they distrust the technology and fear it will not work.

When a monthly payment rises although the account is in credit, help an account holder judge whether the increase is justified and how to stop overpaying, while the supplier controls both the forecast and the balance.
